name: Monkey puzzles and their kin
notes: The Araucaria trees of Gondwana: monkey puzzle of the Andes, Paraná pine of Brazil, bunya of Queensland, Norfolk Island pine, and the Cook pine — dinosaur-age conifers with armoured leaves and huge cones. Landmark trees; bunya nuts fed gatherings.

emergent.name: Kauri

growth.juvenile_note: Young kauri ('rickers') are narrow cones with branches along the whole trunk. Juvenile leaves are 5-10 cm long, lance-shaped and olive-green to bronze or red, much larger than the 2-3.5 cm adult leaves. Little height growth for about 5 years, then 30-40 cm a year; lower branches drop later to leave a clean columnar trunk.
growth.source: Tane's Trees Trust kauri guide (germination 2-3 wk, 30 cm at 1 yr, 10-40 cm/yr, viable seed at 25-40 yr, juvenile leaves 5-10 cm, 2 m trees ~1100 yr); Steward & Beveridge 2014 NZ J For Sci (22 m at age 60, slow first 5 yr); Gymnosperm Database (0.35 m/yr; fertile seed at 25-30 yr)

emergent.source: Northland, New Zealand; vast grey columns; the same family. Kew POWO.

traits.trunk: towering straight bole, buttressed base, crown above the canopy
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: smooth grey-blue-mauve bark shedding in thick hammer-marked flakes, leaving a mottled patchwork of grey, cream and rust; huge resin drips

leaf.notes: thick leathery oblong to lance leaves, blunt, parallel-veined; bronze-red juvenile foliage; dull mid green adult

flower.form: cylindrical tan pollen cones 2-5 cm; round green female cones

fruit.form: round green cones 5-7 cm ripening brown, disintegrate on the tree

appearance.silhouette: a colossal grey untapered column bare for 20 m, then a massive rounded broad crown of thick radiating limbs; a forest cathedral pillar
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Agathis australis; NZ Plant Conservation Network; Kew POWO

fruiting.source: Gymnosperm Database (conifers.org): pollen cones 2-5 cm; seed cones subglobose 5-7.5 cm, glaucous green; pollination in October, seed mature Feb-Mar of the second year after (19-20 months); cones break up on the tree releasing winged seeds; fertile seed from 25-30 yr

canopy.name: Monkey puzzle

growth.juvenile_note: Seed germinates hypogeally; the stout shoot bears overlapping, rigid, glossy, triangular, sharp leaves. For decades saplings are a broad, symmetrical dark green cone with regular whorls of 5-7 rope-like branches armoured in spiny leaves right down to the ground. Lower branches are later shed, leaving a tall bare trunk under an umbrella-like crown.
growth.source: Wikipedia EN (30-40 m; no seed until ~30-40 yr; ages beyond 1,000 yr; young trees broadly pyramidal; seedlings do best in canopy gaps), Wikipedia ES (first seed ~25 yr, precocious 15; pollen Dec-Jan) and Gymnosperm Database (834-ring sample; ~1,300-yr report). Height-age curve and germination days estimated (very slow growth).

canopy.source: Chilean and Argentine Andes on volcanic ash; sacred to the Mapuche; 1,000 years. Kew POWO.

bark.notes: grey-brown bark in horizontal ridged rings and wrinkles (like elephant hide), old leaf scars persisting; resin-crusted

leaf.notes: thick, stiff, glossy triangular scale leaves with a sharp spine tip, overlapping spirally to sheath the whole branch like reptile scales

flower.form: long cylindrical tan pollen cones; round spiky female cones

fruit.form: big round cones 10-18 cm, green then brown, shatter; large edible nuts

appearance.silhouette: straight trunk with whorls of rope-like, upcurved snakey branches; young trees a full pyramid, old trees a bare pole with a flat-topped umbrella of tufts
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Araucaria araucana; Kew POWO; Gymnosperm Database

fruiting.source: Wikipedia EN/ES and Gymnosperm Database: mostly dioecious, pollen shed Dec-Jan from 7-15 cm pollen cones; globular dark brown seed cones 12-20 cm mature ~15-18 months after pollination (seeds ripe Mar-Apr), breaking up to release ~200 seeds 3-4 cm (pinones), eaten boiled or roasted and spread by grass mice and parakeets. Crop estimated.

canopy.name: Paraná pine

growth.juvenile_note: The big seed (pinhao) germinates hypogeally, staying in the soil while a stout shoot rises with spirally set, stiff, sharp-pointed, triangular lance leaves 3-6 cm. Saplings are neat symmetrical cones adding a whorl of 4-8 horizontal branches each year, leaves crowded toward the branch tips. The flat-topped candelabra crown forms only after decades as lower whorls drop.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Araucaria angustifolia: usually to 40 m; up to 16 m in 14 yr in plantation; leaves 3-6 cm, persist 10-15 yr) and Gymnosperm Database (25-35(-52) m; max ca. 500 yr; hypogeal germination, 2 cotyledons). Germination days, first coning (~12-20 yr) and shade class estimated from Brazilian forestry accounts.

canopy.source: S Brazilian highlands; candelabra crown; pine-nut forests. Kew POWO.

bark.notes: thick dark grey-brown to red-brown bark, scaly and shallowly furrowed, flaking in thin plates; resinous

leaf.notes: narrow stiff lance-shaped scale leaves, sharp-tipped, dark green, spiralling densely round the branch tips

flower.form: cylindrical tan pollen cones; round female cones

fruit.form: big round cones 10-25 cm, green to brown, of large edible pinhao nuts

appearance.silhouette: the candelabra: tall bare trunk topped by a flat, wide umbrella of long upturned branches ending in tufts; unmistakable in the southern Brazilian highlands
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Araucaria angustifolia; Kew POWO; Gymnosperm Database

fruiting.source: Wikipedia and Gymnosperm Database: usually dioecious and wind-pollinated; pollen cones 10-18 cm; globose chestnut-brown seed cones 18-25 cm (~1 kg or more) mature in autumn ~18 months after pollination and hold 100-150 seeds ~5 cm long, eaten boiled or roasted and spread by azure jays. Pollination months and crop estimated.

canopy.name: Bunya pine

growth.juvenile_note: Germination is cryptogeal: the seed first sends down a root that swells into a carrot-like underground tuber, and the shoot emerges from it typically 7-11 months (2-24) after sowing. Saplings are dark glossy symmetrical cones, whorls of branches clothed in narrow, glossy, light green, sharp spreading leaves 2.5-5 cm; old trees carry short overlapping leaves and a dome of branches at the top.
growth.source: Gymnosperm Database (Araucaria bidwillii: to 50 m; cones from ~14 yr; hypogeal cryptogeal germination via a tuber, emergence 2-(7-11)-24 months after sowing; juvenile leaves glossy, narrow, 2.5-5 cm vs adult 0.7-2.8 cm; masts ~every 3 yr) and Wikipedia (lives ~500 yr). Height-age curve and shade class estimated.

canopy.source: Queensland; football-sized cones; the bunya feasts. Kew POWO.

fruiting.source: Gymnosperm Database and Wikipedia: pollen cones to 20 cm mature Sep-Nov; rugby-ball seed cones ~30 x 22 cm, up to 10 kg, fall whole Dec-Mar about 17-18 months after pollination, each with 50-100 nuts 2.5-5 cm (chestnut-like, eaten raw or roasted); heavy crops ~every 3 yr. Crop per tree estimated.

canopy.name: Norfolk Island pine

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings and saplings carry soft, bright green, incurved awl-shaped needles 10-15 mm. The young tree is the classic near-perfect pyramid for its first ~40 years: tiers of about five horizontal branches, each floor a neat star, with frond-like branchlets in whorls of 4-7. Adult crowns flatten and carry short, overlapping, incurved scale leaves 5-10 mm.
growth.source: Gymnosperm Database (Araucaria heterophylla: 50-70 m; female cones on trees >15 yr, male cones >40 yr; heavy seed fall every 4-5 yr; oldest documented 170 yr; almost symmetrical for ~40 yr) and Wikipedia (slow-growing, 50-65 m; juvenile leaves awl-shaped 10-15 mm vs adult 5-10 mm). Germination days and height-age estimated.

canopy.source: Norfolk Island coasts; tiered symmetrical whorls. Kew POWO.
